source: Dr. Thaveesak Sangudom, Dr. Theerawut Chutinanthakun, and Wirot Horasart, "Off-season Production Techniques for Pursat Orange (ក្រូចពោធិ៍សាត់ / kroch poursat) in Cambodia," in The Guideline of Climate Change Adaptation in Cambodia (pp. 130-153), Project on Promoting Climate Resilience in Farming Communities of Cambodia, General Department of Agriculture (GDA) Cambodia, Thailand International Cooperation Agency (TICA), and Department of Agriculture (DOA) Thailand, 2017-2020.
text:
The best-quality indicator used for deciding when to harvest Pursat orange is total soluble solids / sugar content (TSS), with a minimum target of 9% TSS. In the demonstration orchard following this program's techniques, harvested fruit measured 11-13% TSS, compared with only 9-10% TSS typically measured in ordinary orchards not using these techniques. This sugar-content comparison is reported twice in the source (once in the main technique description and again in the results summary), with matching figures both times.

The harvest itself, plus sorting by size/grade and packing, is scheduled across August-September in the annual production calendar, with record-keeping of the season's results done in the final week of the cycle.
